featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
MM Mithaiwala was once considered one of the go-to snack spots in its prime years — a place people would specially visit for chaat and mithai. Over time, however, it feels like it has settled into being more of a familiar, comforting neighbourhood stop rather than a standout destination. When I visited recently, it felt reliable and comforting, but not particularly memorable.

Recently tried their batata vada, samosa, and a few of the other popular dishes from the menu.

Over the years, MM has been known for its wide variety, and you’ll find almost everything here under one roof. Some popular picks worth trying include:
•	Dahi Kachori – nicely assembled with sweet and spicy chutneys, fairly typical in flavour.
•	Pani Puri & Sev Puri – good hygiene and presentation, classic sweet-tangy balance, but similar to what you’ll get at most good chaat counters across the city.
•	Khaman Dhokla – soft and fresh, mildly sweet as expected.
•	Kachori – flaky outer crust with decent stuffing, best enjoyed warm.
•	Jalebi & Fafda – especially during festive mornings, fresh and satisfying.
•	Assorted Mithai & Dryfruit Sweets – vast range, neatly displayed, standard quality.

The place remains clean and efficient, making it convenient for a quick bite or takeaway. Overall, it’s dependable and comforting, but the flavours feel quite ordinary — something you can easily find at many corners of Mumbai today.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience this Diwali specially for Gift package had got for my staff. What was sad was after sale feedback.

Gift boxes had Red ants on box aliveas well as dead so as soon as 1 of my staff reported I asked to throw them but then too thought to preserve 1 box cover as proof a d to share feedback on episode I faced .. It's first time ever since 2012 since I became regular customer f J k sweets Malad. This time I bought it from Mahavir nagar and faced this unpleasant experience.
Instead of understanding issue and bad gifting experience they expect to bring back sweet boxes with Ants 🐜 .. Bad state of affairs.. Atleast understand customer sentiment specially when they are giving gift it's sad to see such non practical feedback.

It's not just about money but atleast value trust of customer who have blind faith in your business.

Whish you wisdom and better sense of understanding.

Good bye J k !
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We’re truly sorry to hear about your experience and understand how upsetting it must have been, especially during Diwali when gifts carry so much sentiment. Please know that we take quality very seriously and have not received such complaints about ants before. However, we acknowledge that it’s possible and are committed to addressing any quality issues with our products.

In your case, I understand that you threw away the sweets due to the ants. But please try to see it from our perspective: our team needs some form of evidence to process a refund—if not the product itself, then at least a photo showing the issue with the product. Even major companies like Amazon require returns or evidence to issue refunds—how can my employee issue a refund or replacement without it? He could risk losing his job, and I’m sure you wouldn’t want him to be in that position over a situation like this. This is not about distrust, but about ensuring a fair and systematic refund process for everyone involved.

We deeply value your loyalty over the years and apologize for any inconvenience caused. We’d be happy to discuss alternative ways to make this right. Thank you for your feedback, and we hope to restore your faith in us.

Thier staff does not take proper care of hygienic. If we say something to them, they simply reply us , go inside the shop & complaint, whomever u want to.

Thier Dhokla can be used as a stone to hurt somebody. It's super stiff ,they make it super heavy cause it is selling  by weight . they don't have control over quality. Careless management.
Whenever u land to that shop , staff are always spending time with thier cellphones.

They never provide fried chillies with thier snacks, which is customers right to ask .

Pathetic management & services .

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the very oldest Jain Farsan Shop in Malad West, since decades the Mohanlal & Sons serving different varieties of farsan especially the delicious mouth watering Faafda & Jalebi with Papaya & Yellow Khaman sambhra.

Though it's costly but people who are foodies they will not see the price due to it's exotic taste.

Usually on Sunday's if you are planning to get Faafda & Jalebi for early breakfast, then please plan accordingly and visit early morning by 7:00 am to get it hot and fresh, as the hours passes through, the one have to stand in a long queue but no worries as the Faafda's and Jalebi's are served hot and fresh, so to avoid the long queue, plan accordingly.

As per the rates of the farsan, as a foodie, I don't feel that it's really that tasty.

Rates for sweets and farsan differs on timely basis and seasonal too.

Staffs members are ok and neither helpful.

Overall, it's worth to spend the money if your going for taste only once.
